input.raw_text: Repo went vertical this week: overnight funds printed near ten percent intraday and the effective fed funds rate broke above the target range, something I have not seen since the crisis-era plumbing debates. The Fed responded with overnight and term repo operations, lending reserves against Treasuries and MBS — the first such injections in years. The proximate culprits are corporate tax dates and a large Treasury settlement draining cash, but underneath it feels structural: bill supply has ballooned, reserves look scarcer than the Fed assumed, and quarter-end is bearing down. Funding desks are nervous, bid-ask in bills is wide, and I would not be surprised if the central bank keeps supplying liquidity through month-end while it studies the reserve question.
input.summary: Repo funding rates surged to nearly ten percent intraday, and the effective federal funds rate moved above its target range. The Federal Reserve responded with overnight and term repo operations against Treasuries and agency MBS. Corporate tax payments and a large Treasury settlement appear to have drained near-term cash, while expanded bill supply, scarcer-than-expected reserves, and approaching quarter-end pressures suggest a possible structural funding imbalance. Funding desks appear uneasy, Treasury bill bid-ask spreads are wide, and continued central-bank liquidity provision through month-end remains possible but uncertain.
